solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Clot's way to get into clue cracking

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it, so one piece sits within another
something cracking breaks apart, so its letters are smashed and reassembled in a new order

blocks.note: the four letters of the word as printed, to be rearranged
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A setter's idiotic way of breaking into a cryptic clue, with clot as the British insult for a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clot' reads as an insult (a clot is a fool), but it is the verb, and the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk or blood that clots thickens into lumps, and curdling is exactly that thickening process.

clue.text: Phwoar! £1! That's official

blocks.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise or admiration, like phwoar
a oner is British slang for a pound or a one-pound note

explanation.surface: Someone leering at a bargain priced at a pound, declaring it official.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are British slang: cor is an exclamation like 'wow', and a oner is a pound coin or note.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner is a public officer who investigates sudden or unexplained deaths, so the role is an official one.

clue.text: A sort of dash, in drunken fluster, for bitter

indicators.note: a drunken person staggers about, so the letters lurch out of order
placed in something means set inside it, enclosed by the other letters

blocks.note: the seven letters as printed, to be scrambled
an en dash is a typographical dash the width of a letter N

explanation.surface: A tipsy, flustered person dashing off to the pub for a pint of bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' looks like the beer, a British pale ale, but it is the adjective. 'Dash' is typographical, not a sprint.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bitter nurses a grievance and feels aggrieved, which is the same feeling of sour indignation.

clue.text: Honolulu creamed housing cash

indicators.note: a building housing something holds it inside, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: the end of the city name runs into the start of the next word

explanation.surface: Honolulu cleaning up and taking in a pile of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creamed' suggests a thrashing or skimming profits, but it only supplies letters: honoLULU CREamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is an old, usually disparaging word for money, as in 'filthy lucre'.

clue.text: Pressure line one consequently attached to engineered bra

indicators.note: anything engineered has been built or rigged up, so its letters are reconstructed

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
so means therefore or as a result
the three letters as printed, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An engineered bra exerting pressure along one line, a joke about underwiring.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all lingerie; 'Pressure line' is the weather-map definition at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather chart an isobar is a contour joining places of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Understanding "commie" being furious

blocks.note: to see is to understand, as in 'I see what you mean'
a red is a communist

explanation.surface: Grasping that someone has been branded a commie and getting angry about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase, matching the -ING form of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is an idiom for losing your temper, as a bull supposedly charges at a red cape.

clue.text: Focus of Tony Blair is on papers, which is altogether fishy

definitions.note: an extended definition: the whole result is a fish

indicators.note: a focus is a central point, so only the middle letter is kept

blocks.note: the fifth of nine letters in the full name
a ream is a pack of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: The former Prime Minister's preoccupation with the newspapers, a whole business that smells fishy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Focus of Tony Blair' points at the centre of the full name, not of BLAIR alone. 'Altogether fishy' insinuates spin, but it tells you the answer is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The bream is a deep-bodied freshwater or sea fish, so the finished word names something fishy.

clue.text: Bigots: "It's about terrorist organisation being embraced by assholes"

indicators.note: whatever is embraced is held in someone's arms, so it sits inside the outer letters

blocks.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
IS is the abbreviation for the jihadist group Islamic State
rats are contemptible, treacherous people

explanation.surface: Someone labelling bigots as a sort of terror cell shielded by unpleasant people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' is easy to read as a reversal signal here, but it is just C, for circa, joined to IS before both go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigot is intolerant of other groups, and racists are a common kind of such prejudiced people.

clue.text: Opportunity for Trump to attack questioners and urge party, er, to go into Wall alternative?

definitions.text: Opportunity for Trump to attack questioners

indicators.note: going into something means entering it, so these letters are placed inside another word

blocks.note: to press someone is to urge them
Con is short for the Conservative Party
taken as written
a fence is a cheaper barrier than a border wall

explanation.surface: Trump at a podium rounding on reporters while hesitating over a fence instead of his promised border wall.
explanation.walkthrough: The hesitant 'er' is a real piece, not filler. Con is the standard short form for the British Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: At a press conference journalists put questions to a public figure, which Trump used to berate reporters.

clue.text: (& 11ac.) Amnesty broadcast with two seconds description of Brexit situation?

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, like seed thrown about, so the letters are dispersed

blocks.note: the seven letters as printed
S is the abbreviation for second, taken twice

explanation.surface: Amnesty International going on air for two seconds to sum up how Brexit is going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suggests radio or TV, but here it means scattered. The question mark flags a jokey, opinionated definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An unpleasant muddle or shambles, a fair if partisan way to characterise the political chaos around leaving the EU.

clue.text: Macron's end is linked to working with sex-grabbing, former president, who's out of favour, politically

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept
something grabbing clutches hold of another thing, so it wraps around those letters

blocks.note: the French president's name ends in this letter
a machine that is on is working
Juan Perón was president of Argentina
S is short for sex, as on a form

explanation.surface: Macron linked with a sex-grabbing former president who has fallen from grace, a jibe at Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex-grabbing former president' points to Trump, but the president here is Perón of Argentina, and he does the grabbing of S.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-person is someone officially ignored or erased from record, typically a disgraced figure in an authoritarian regime.

clue.text: see 9dn.
Democrats leader cracks and goes off course

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the party name
rifts are cracks or splits

explanation.surface: The Democrats' leader cracks under pressure and the party loses its way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracks' reads as a verb about the leader breaking, but it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that drifts is carried by currents and wanders from its intended heading.

clue.text: Action hero sprained balls, going round mountain top

indicators.note: to balls something up is British slang for botching it, so the letters are jumbled
going round something encircles it, so these letters enclose another
the top of a down entry word is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the eight letters as printed, to be scrambled
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A film hero injuring his testicles while running around a summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sprained balls' looks like an injury; SPRAINED is the fodder and 'balls' the signal. To balls up is British slang for to mess up.
explanation.definitionFit: Spider-Man is the Marvel comic and film superhero, the very model of an action hero.

clue.text: They give easy access to a member

definitions.text: They give easy access to a member

blocks.clueFragment: They give easy access to a member
blocks.note: surface reading: an organisation or club that makes joining simple for members
setter's reading: the member is the male organ, and the garment has a front opening for it

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a club's open admissions policy; 'member' is the cheeky double meaning. Y-fronts are British men's briefs with an inverted-Y fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Men's underpants of this style have an overlapping front opening, a fly that lets the wearer get at himself easily.

clue.text: The chief leak

blocks.note: first meaning: the boss, the person at the top
second meaning: a child's word for urinating, since a leak is slang for a pee

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a news story about the boss leaking secrets; in fact 'leak' is British slang for a pee, as in 'take a leak'.
explanation.definitionFit: The top person is the head boss, and in nursery language a wee is distinguished from the other business by a numeral.

clue.text: Private association of The Sun with dire consequences

indicators.note: consequences are the things that follow on from a change, so the letters are altered into a new order

blocks.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
the four letters as printed, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A private dealing with The Sun tabloid ends disastrously, a nod to phone-hacking and Private Eye itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an adjective about secrecy, or Private Eye; it is the army rank. The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, but here it is just SOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A private is the lowest rank in the army, so any private is a serving soldier.

clue.text: Run down two fellows east of Lagos, being pissed

indicators.note: pissed is British slang for drunk, and a drunk's letters stagger out of order
east of something lies to its right, so these letters come after the others

blocks.note: the five letters of the city name as printed
F is the abbreviation for fellow, taken twice

explanation.surface: Two drunk men in Nigeria's biggest city, worn out and staggering east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run down' looks like 'exhausted' but is the verb meaning to criticise. Pissed is British for drunk, not angry.
explanation.definitionFit: To slag off is British slang for to criticise someone harshly, the same as running them down.

clue.text: see 20ac.
Get rid of mater and all she commands?

definitions.note: the realm a ruler controls; the 'she' ties it to mater

blocks.note: to do in is to kill, to get rid of someone
mater is Latin for mother, and ma is the short familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A plot to bump off mother and take over everything she rules.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no container signal: the two-word phrasal verb simply splits to let mother in. Mater is posh British slang for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is the territory or realm under someone's control, everything over which they hold sway.

clue.text: The woman's into trendy sex, so come by!

indicators.note: going into something means entering it, so these letters sit inside the others

blocks.note: her belongs to a woman
in means fashionable
it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A woman keen on fashionable sex extends an invitation to drop round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come by' reads as an invitation to visit; it means to acquire. 'Sex' is the coy 'it' of 'doing it'.
explanation.definitionFit: To come by something is to obtain it, and receiving property from someone who has died is one way of acquiring it.

clue.text: (& 17dn.) Aroused appropriate extremist element

blocks.note: a crude word for sexually aroused, in the male sense
right means proper or fitting

explanation.surface: An excited, fitting reaction from the radical fringe of politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' could be the verb meaning seize, but here it is the adjective, fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: The far end of the conservative spectrum is the faction holding the most radical, uncompromising views.

clue.text: Bandit-type housing shanty?

indicators.note: a house holds things inside, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A bandit holed up in a shack, as if shanty meant a shanty town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shanty' looks like a ramshackle hut for a bandit to live in; it is the sailor's song.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea shanty is a work song sung by sailors, and a ditty is any short simple song.

clue.text: Special occasion? Mass doesn't start before one? The bastard!

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for an eightieth birthday or anniversary

indicators.note: a word that doesn't start has lost its opening letter
coming before means going first, so these letters are placed ahead of the next
a bastard is illegitimate, not a true product, so the letters come out corrupted

blocks.note: weight is mass, and losing its opening letter leaves this
the Roman numeral for one
the three letters as printed

explanation.surface: Someone missing church on a special day and cursing the person responsible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' suggests the church service, but it is weight in the physics sense, beheaded to EIGHT. 'The bastard!' looks like an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: An eightieth birthday or anniversary is a landmark celebration, so the ordinal stands in for that occasion.

clue.text: Swells? Embarrassingly soft when female enters

indicators.note: done embarrassingly is done awkwardly and wrongly, so the letters end up in a different order
entering means going inside, so this letter is placed within the others

blocks.note: the four letters as printed, to be rearranged
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: An awkward swelling that goes soft when a woman walks in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swells' reads as a verb about bodily swelling; it is the plural noun for posh people. Toffs is the British term for upper-class people.
explanation.definitionFit: A swell is a dated word for a fashionable, well-off person, and toffs are British slang for the upper class.

clue.text: Scam by Trump, etc: "Foot distorted Tommy Robinson's wrongdoing"

indicators.note: a distorted thing is twisted out of shape, so these letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: a con is a swindle
the letters of the three words as printed, to be scrambled

explanation.surface: A swindle by Trump and his kind, with someone claiming a far-right activist's crime has been twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Robinson, an English far-right activist, was jailed in 2018 for contempt after filming outside a trial. 'Foot' is just letters, not a unit or body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinson's offence was disobeying a court reporting restriction, and defying a judge's order is this specific legal crime.

clue.text: May's final fling's all over, in the air

indicators.note: the final part of a word is its last letter, so only that is kept
something all over another covers it on every side, so it wraps around those letters

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of the Prime Minister's surname

explanation.surface: Theresa May's last fling has ended, with everything still up in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All over' sounds like 'finished', for May's premiership, but it tells the letters of the fling to spread over the final letter of her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something airborne and travelling through the sky is flying, held aloft rather than on the ground.

clue.text: Thumbs up Trump's behind – not much amusement

indicators.note: not much of a word means only a little of it survives, so most letters are dropped

blocks.note: ass is American slang for the backside
only the closing three letters are left once the front is cut away

explanation.surface: Giving a thumbs-up to Trump's backside offers little to laugh at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump's behind' reads as 'supporting Trump'; it is his rear. Only a scrap of 'amusement' survives, its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbs-up is a gesture of approval or agreement, and giving consent is expressing that agreement.
